title: The Tears of the Scribe
next_chapter_hook: The Tianji Record began its qualitative transformation in Chen Ji's hands, that radiance transcending fate causing all heaven and earth to tremble—and this was merely a beginning.

text.content: The lingering echo of the dissipating remnant soul had not yet faded. Chen Ji stood within the void, surrounded by the reverberations of his father's words. Go see your mother's true face—like a key, yet one that opened onto unknown forbidden doors. He slowly turned, gazing at the figure woven from countless threads of fate. The Eye of Heavenly Dao, or in other words, the Scribe of Destiny, now gazed quietly at him. Within those eyes were reflected the birth and death of billions of stars, yet they alone could not see through the fate of this trash disciple.

"You heard." Chen Ji's voice was terrifyingly calm, as if the scene of life and death moments ago was someone else's affair, "My father said for me to go see my mother's face. A face erased by the Heavenly Dao." He paused, the corner of his lips curling into a mocking arc, "I presume this is the work of your Heavenly Dao?" The threads of fate trembled slightly at the Scribe's fingertips, and on that face composed of light, a crack called wavering appeared for the first time.

dialogue.content: "...Yes." The Scribe of Destiny's voice was no longer the cold arrogance from before, but carried an undetectable exhaustion, "That face will let you see the truth. But before that—" He raised his hand, countless threads of fate unfurling behind him like an unrolled scroll of destiny, "There are some things I want to tell you myself."

text.content: Chen Ji narrowed his eyes. Having played the pig to devour the tiger for years, he had long grown accustomed to捕捉破绽 from the slightest details. The Scribe of Destiny's current posture was far too unusual—the slightly lowered eyelids, the suppressed aura, the silence of standing in place without taking the initiative to strike. What was he waiting for? Or rather... what was he hesitating about? Chen Ji's thoughts raced, yet his expression remained unchanged, simply standing with hands clasped behind his back as if watching a drama that had nothing to do with him.

dialogue.content: "Do you think I have never regretted?" The Scribe of Destiny suddenly spoke, his voice carrying a hint of self-mockery, "Billions of years, billions of reincarnations, billions of fates I wove with my own hands... You think I am the Heavenly Dao, but in truth, I am merely a prisoner." His gaze fell upon the Tianji Record in Chen Ji's hand, and deep in his eyes, some light was swaying, "And the thing in your hands—that was the only thing I ever wanted to grasp."

text.content: The void quivered. The Scribe of Destiny's figure began to blur, as if some kind of shackle was loosening. Chen Ji's pupils contracted—what did he see? In the depths of those countless threads of fate, a youthful silhouette was slowly emerging. It was a face he had never seen before, yet one that filled him with an inexplicable familiarity. Was this... what the Scribe looked like before becoming the Heavenly Dao? Chen Ji swallowed the surge of inexplicable emotion, his voice cold: "What's the point of saying all this? Trying to make me soft?"

dialogue.content: "No." The Scribe of Destiny shook his head, and on that gradually clarifying face, a crystalline point of light appeared—a tear, a tear of destiny transcending material form, "I only wanted you to know that when I returned to the past to stop myself, it wasn't entirely for the continuation of the Heavenly Dao." He raised his head, gazing directly at Chen Ji with a level stare for the first time, "It's because I didn't want to see... anyone else be like me, carried along by fate toward the abyss."

text.content: The tears fell, dissolving into stardust upon touching the void. Chen Ji was stunned. He had witnessed the Scribe's might, the cold ruthlessness of the Eye of Heavenly Dao, that arrogance of looking down upon all living beings as mere ants—yet never this. The one who had fate dancing between his fingers now resembled a lost child, exposed and with no place to hide. Chen Ji suddenly understood something, his voice slightly hoarse: "You... regret?"

"Regret?" The Scribe of Destiny laughed lightly, that laughter carrying an indescribable bitterness, "Billions of years of regret. What I regret isn't becoming the Heavenly Dao, but that moment when I became the Heavenly Dao—I personally erased my own emotions." He raised his hand, condensing a small orb of light at his fingertips, within which flowed the core code of the Tianji Record, "This... originally belonged to you. I seized it from the first generation prophet, and now... I return it to you."

choice.prompt: The Scribe of Destiny offered the core code of the Tianji Record to Chen Ji—this was the key to opening the fourth path. But Chen Ji's mood at this moment was incomparably complex—with what kind of attitude should he face this sudden "gift"?

choices.description: The Scribe of Destiny's regret was genuine, and Chen Ji decided to no longer pursue the past. Instead, he chose to attempt fusing with this power, blazing a brand new path.
choices.visible_cost: Generate a fateful entanglement with the Heavenly Dao's will
choices.visible_reward: Prerequisite conditions for obtaining the complete Tianji Record
choices.risk_hint: The fusion process is extremely perilous; one might lose oneself

text.content: Chen Ji was silent for a moment, then suddenly stepped forward. He didn't reach for the orb of light, but stared directly into the Scribe of Destiny's eyes, word by word: "You're right, the past is the past. Since you're willing to give me this chance, then I shall—" He extended his hand, "Fuse with you, and blaze that fourth path."

choices.memory_label: 与命运书写者的羁绊加深

choices.description: Chen Ji accepted this power, but made it clear that he would transcend the Scribe of Destiny's regret—he would not repeat this history, but instead surpass all of it.
choices.visible_cost: Need to prove he has this qualification
choices.visible_reward: The Scribe of Destiny gives full support
choices.risk_hint: May provoke the backlash of the Heavenly Dao's will

text.content: Chen Ji took the orb of light, but did not fuse with it immediately. He looked at the Scribe of Destiny, a faint smile curling at his lips: "You speak as if I'm destined to regret. Rest assured—when I, Chen Ji, do something, I never leave regrets." The words fell, and the orb of light was drawn into the Tianji Record. With a thunderous rumble, the entire void trembled.

choices.memory_label: 展现了超越天道的决心

choices.description: Chen Ji believed that the sins of the Heavenly Eye could not be erased with mere "regret"—he intended to die alongside this existence that had once harmed his family.
choices.visible_cost: Give up the chance to open the Fourth Path
choices.risk_hint: May lead to a situation where both sides suffer

text.content: Chen Ji did not take it. His gaze turned cold and sharp, as if looking at a corpse: "Regret? If you're sorry, will my mother come back? Will my father's scattered soul reform?" He forcefully activated the Tianji Record, a devastating power gathering at his fingertips. "Billions of years of sins—how dare you think a single apology can wash them away? Come, let us die together."

The moment the orb of light merged with the Tianji Record, Chen Ji's mind exploded with thunderous noise. Countless images flooded in like a tide—those were the Writer of Destiny's billion-year memories, his struggles as a mortal, his loneliness after becoming the Heavenly Dao, and the unending fire of regret that never extinguished through those endless years. Chen Ji saw his younger self standing at fate's crossroads, making the choice that changed everything.

dialogue.content: "Do you see it now?" The Writer of Destiny's voice rang in Chen Ji's mind, no longer external words but a soul-level resonance. "I too had the chance to choose the Fourth Path back then, but fear blinded my eyes." The voice trembled. "So I know better than anyone... you can do what I could not. Please... end this damned cycle of fate."

text.content: Chen Ji closed his eyes tightly, letting those memories not belonging to him surge through his consciousness. He saw the Writer of Destiny's former beloved, the truth erased by the Heavenly Dao, the "I'm sorry" that was never spoken even unto death. After an unknown passage of time, he slowly opened his eyes to find his face streaked with tears. He wiped away the tears, his voice hoarse yet firm: "I答应你."

choice.prompt: The Tianji Record began to transform, emanating radiance that transcended fate. At this moment, Chen Ji needed to decide the purpose of this power—would it be used for restoration, or for destruction?

choices.description: Use this power to restore the history corrupted by the Heavenly Dao—including his mother's memories, as well as countless sacrificed seers.
choices.visible_cost: Consume a massive amount of Heavenly Fate
choices.risk_hint: May trigger the Heavenly Dao Law's backlash

text.content: Chen Ji took a deep breath, guiding that power toward the shattered nodes of history. In an instant, countless points of light bloomed in the void, like stars across the heavens being relit. He saw his mother's blurry face gradually becoming clear, those eyes so like his own finally regaining their brilliance. "Mother..." he murmured, his voice carrying warmth he had never known before.

choices.description: Transform all power into a strike of destruction, thoroughly annihilating the foundation of the Heavenly Eye, fundamentally rewriting the laws of destiny.
choices.visible_cost: The Tianji Record may collapse as a result
choices.visible_reward: The Heavenly Eye is completely annihilated
choices.risk_hint: May trigger an even greater catastrophe

text.content: Chen Ji's gaze hardened, and the Tianji Record in his palm erupted with unprecedented radiance. It was power enough to tear apart the heavens, the total eruption of anger and sorrow accumulated across countless years. "Since you've given me this chance—" he hurled the light toward the Writer of Destiny, "then let your destruction serve as an offering to all those you sacrificed!"

Just then, an abrupt voice rang through the void: "Interesting." Chen Ji's heart jolted, and he spun around—Cang Yutian's figure had somehow appeared nearby, hands clasped behind his back, gazing over with a meaningful smile playing at his lips. "This is the true variable." His gaze shifted between Chen Ji and the Writer of Destiny, something being kindled in the depths of his eyes. "It seems this game... is more interesting than I imagined."

dialogue.content: Chen Ji narrowed his eyes, placing Cang Yutian on his list of those to be wary of. This person's presence was far too strange—they always appeared at the most critical moments yet never directly intervened. Was he enemy or ally? Or perhaps... did he have other schemes? But this was not the time for deeper investigation. Chen Ji withdrew his gaze, looking at the Writer of Destiny who was gradually fading before him, his voice low: "What else do you have to say?"

"Go." The Writer of Destiny's form had become nearly transparent, but his voice was gentler than ever before. "Go see your mother, find your sister, end all of this." A serene smile appeared on his face—it was an expression Chen Ji had never seen before, almost human. "Remember... the Fourth Path does not lie within fate, but in the heart of every living being. What you must do is let them choose for themselves."

text.content: The final wisp of light dissipated, and the Writer of Destiny completely faded into the void. Yet the Tianji Record in Chen Ji's hand erupted with dazzling brilliance at this moment—no longer the fragmented, fate-bound radiance, but a completely new existence that transcended destiny. Countless prophetic visions that had been blurry were now becoming clear; the Fourth Path had finally opened before him. And simultaneously, he felt a seal in his mind beginning to loosen—what was this... memories of his mother?

Chen Ji slowly raised the Tianji Record, feeling the brand-new power flowing through his body. The ability to foresee the future remained, but this time, it was no longer a one-sided glimpse—he saw possible futures, and also the possibility of changing those futures. A faint smile curved his lips as Chen Ji murmured: "The fourth path... so that's how it is." He turned, gazing toward where Cang Yutian was, his eyes deep and dark as an abyss. This chess game was far more complex than he had imagined. But Chen Ji had never feared complexity. "Let's go," he said to the void, "It's time to go meet my mother."
